source_title: Sridhar Vembu says only humans with meta level skills will benefit from AI - India Today
source_excerpt:
As Sridhar Vembu points out, true job security now lies in mastering the "meta-level" skills to keep the machine on track.
Artificial intelligence is rapidly changing the way modern offices function, and it is creating a noticeable divide between employees who use it and those who do not. Zoho CEO Sridhar Vembu has sparked a fresh conversation around Artificial Intelligence in the modern workplace, pointing out a new reality for desk jobs.
Taking to X (formerly Twitter), Vembu stated that any computer-based job now carries a specific risk: "one smart person using AI can perform the work of 10 people." This statement triggered a thoughtful exchange on the platform, highlighting how AI is not just speeding up tasks but fundamentally dividing the workforce into two very different categories of employees. advertisement ❮ ❯ Read Full Story The Rise of the Hyper-Productive Worker The conversation expanded when user Sindhu Hariharan replied to Vembu's initial post, pointing out a fascinating trend happening in offices right now. According to her observation, professionals who successfully integrate AI into their daily line of work actually tend to get busier. Because they can do more at a faster pace, they end up taking on greater responsibilities. On the flip side, Hariharan noted that employees who ignore AI tools for productivity are "still happily taking things slow." She called this a major workplace shift that corporate teams will soon have to get used to. AI Demands 'Meta-Level' Skills Responding to Hariharan's observation, Vembu agreed and broke down exactly what makes an AI user so much more productive. He explained that getting the most out of AI is not an automatic process; it requires a very specific set of human abilities. To make AI work effectively, Vembu said users must clearly state what they want, which means the person actually needs to understand their own goals first. Next, they must be able to break complex problems into smaller, manageable chunks before feeding them to the AI. Finally, human oversight is crucial to detect when the AI goes off-track and quickly bring it back on the rails.

As technology continues to evolve, the gap between those who use AI to scale their output and those who stick to traditional methods will likely become a defining feature of the modern corporate environment.
